name: Appeal to Emotion
shortDef: Using stirred-up feelings in place of reasons to win agreement.
definition: Trying to make a claim seem true or a choice seem right by provoking feelings such as pride, guilt, disgust, outrage or loyalty, when those feelings don't bear on whether the claim holds up.
howToSpot: Strip out the emotional words; is there still a reason left?
Ask what evidence would support this if you felt nothing about it
Notice vivid imagery, guilt or pride doing the work that facts should do
classicExample: Picture your daughter's face on her birthday. You can't put a price on that, so the deluxe package it is.
legitimateVersion: Emotion is fair when it's proportionate and rides on real reasons, like telling one student's story alongside the cost data, so the feeling motivates the argument instead of replacing it.

contrast.fal_appeal_to_pity: Appeal to emotion can use any feeling; appeal to pity specifically asks for sympathy for someone's hardship.
contrast.fal_appeal_to_fear: Appeal to emotion covers pride, guilt, disgust and more; appeal to fear works by making you afraid of a threat.
